findings.reason: a node following the reader list would wire pace_replay through effective_budget and make the replay report the current lifted multiple against past rows, undoing §9's recorded-multiple guarantee.
findings.text: the reader list says "preflight, the picker's offered rows, budget.pace_hold, the dispatch lane advisory, dispatch rows and pace replay ... all compute through it [effective_budget's result]", but `reckon/crew/pace_replay.py` reads the multiple from the recorded row (`("policy", "pace_multiple")`, line 287, built at line 543) and its loader docstring states its input boundary opens "no live pointers, streams, receipts, or configuration layers" (line 52) — replay must keep reporting the multiple that was in force at each dispatch, which is exactly why §9's rows record it; routing replay through the live lift resolution would rewrite history under a lift

findings.reason: splitting the non-lift reserve change into its own node lets each gate prove its own behaviour and keeps a reserve-semantics change from riding on the lift's verdict.
findings.text: §10 bundles two deliverables: the pace lift (record, read-time expiry, reserve release) and a change to bookend-reserve semantics that applies with no lift in force ("Outside a lift, a group whose every member review_excluded_backends lists withholds no bookend reserve ... This deliberately changes the reserve that §4 landed"), with the done-when asserting the second independently at line 1950 ("With no lift, a group whose members are all review-excluded withholds no bookend reserve"); the two ship on separate mechanisms and pass or fail on separate assertions, so one node cannot be reviewed and closed on one verdict
